svg.aria-label: Build pipeline: four checksummed downloads (driver package, sample root filesystem, public sources, reference toolchain). The rootfs step unpacks the sample filesystem, applies NVIDIA's binaries and creates a login user. The kernel step builds the kernel, NVIDIA's out-of-tree modules and the device trees from public sources and installs them. The image step runs NVIDIA's initrd flash tool without flashing, to generate the flash package. Everything lives in the Linux_for_Tegra directory. The flash step then writes the QSPI-NOR flash and the SD, NVMe or USB drive over USB in recovery mode.
svg.text: What ./build.sh all does: NVIDIA's release in, a flash package out
No SD-card image is assembled. The result is a Linux_for_Tegra/ tree plus the signed images that NVIDIA's tool generates from it.
./build.sh fetch (every file verified against a pinned sha256)
flash tools · firmware binaries · stock kernel
builds signed QSPI images, the APP
rootfs image and the flashing initrd
NVIDIA's own directory layout. Their scripts only work from inside it, so this tree is the real build artifact.
the OS: Ubuntu + NVIDIA userspace + modules
the kernel flashed to the 'kernel' partition
MB1 · MB2 · UEFI · BPMP · SPE … binaries
needs the board in recovery mode
boots a recovery initrd over USB, then writes everything
QSPI-NOR (64 MiB on the module): boot firmware, two copies (A_ and B_)
SD card, NVMe or USB drive: kernel, kernel-dtb, ESP, APP (the root filesystem)
Steps run as your user except where sudo is shown: root-owned files must be created as root. Everything is explained command by command in ./build.sh --dry-run all.
